summary: Okta claim filtering prevents access to internal design system docs site
description:
Issue summary:
Several engineers in the Design Systems team report 403 Access Denied when opening the internal design system documentation site (design-system.redwood.internal) after a recent Okta group sync. Error surface: users authenticated via SSO can sign in but the docs console shows 'You do not have permission to view this page'.

Impact:
- ~8 engineers (design-system team) unable to access docs and component specs during sprint; blocking reviews and demos.
- Affects only staff accounts provisioned/updated during last SCIM sync window (2026-03-09 03:00 UTC).

Environment:
- Prod console behind auth-proxy + OIDC (okta)
- Region: us-west internal network

Observed behavior:
- Users complete Okta SSO and reach console, but receive 403 UI from docs service.
- Auth-proxy logs show token accepted, but RBAC check fails because 'groups' claim appears to be empty or contains sanitized values that don't match internal role mapping.

Expected behavior:
- Groups claim should include team group(s) like 'design-systems' or 'team:design-system' so RBAC maps to the 'docs-viewer' role and grants access.

Urgency/Notes:
- Not a site outage; permissions issue localized to one team and recent user provisioning. Please triage with IAM/SCIM ownership.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a test account provisioned during SCIM sync window (or affected engineer account).
3) Observe redirect to auth-proxy and final 403 UI from docs service after successful login.
4) In auth-proxy logs, decode the ID token and inspect 'groups' claim; verify mismatch against internal mapping table in /etc/rbac/team-mapping.yaml.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Triage: Confirmed replication with affected user. Auth-proxy shows valid JWT but groups claim is a list of single-entry strings with prefixes stripped: e.g., previously 'team:design-system' now shows 'design-system' in some accounts and empty for SCIM-created service accounts.

2026-03-11 11:45 - Hypothesis: New Okta claim filter rule deployed 2026-03-09 removed colon-prefixed namespace tokens during normalization. That causes RBAC lookup to miss keys which are stored with 'team:' prefix in mapping table.

2026-03-12 15:02 - Logs: auth-proxy token decode extract:
  header: <redacted>
  payload snippet: "groups": [] 
  (for user u12345)
  For manager account u67890 groups show ["design-system"] (no namespace).

2026-03-13 08:37 - Cross-checked SCIM provisioning log (okta-scim-sync) for 2026-03-09: group assignments for affected users exist on Okta side. SCIM events show correct group IDs but claim filter transformation likely occurring in Okta token inline hook or assertion rule.

2026-03-13 14:20 - Repro with debug token: created test token via Okta dev console with full group attribute. After applying current org claim filter, token groups returned differ from expected mapping.
comments: Marissa Chen (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Filing this after 2 engineers reported blocked work. Slack thread #support-design-systems contains user screenshots: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234567/p1678456789000000
Aisha Patel (Assignee) - 2026-03-11: Assigned to IAM. Initial triage suggests Okta claim transformation. I will pull the recent Okta rules and compare to our token expectations.

IAM Oncall (internal) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed a claim mutation rule was promoted 2026-03-09 to canonicalize group names (remove characters). Opening Okta change ticket and rollback plan. See Okta change ID CHG-2026-03-09-31.

SRE (observability) - 2026-03-13: Added temporary logging around RBAC key lookup in auth-proxy to capture raw groups payload; no PII logged. Logs stored in splunk at: https://splunk.redwood.com/en-US/app/search?query=source%3Dauth-proxy%20INT-812556

Aisha Patel - 2026-03-14: Action plan: 1) Temporarily relax RBAC mapping to accept both namespaced and non-namespaced group keys; 2) Remove the Okta claim canonicalization rule if rollback approved; 3) Run a targeted resync for affected users. Will coordinate rollback window with SecOps.
Marissa Chen - 2026-03-14: Workaround requested: can we add specific affected users to a temporary 'docs-access-temp' Okta group while fix is implemented? This will unblock reviews.
resolution: In progress: temporary RBAC mapping change prepared and awaiting SecOps approval. IAM prepared rollback of claim rule; temporary Okta group 'docs-access-temp' requested by reporter to be created and populated for affected users to unblock work. Will update when rollback window scheduled.
